ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a grid composed of 3 rows and 3 columns of unit squares. One circle is inscribed in the unit square at the upper left corner, and another circle is inscribed in the unit square at the lower right corner. Reasoning: Each circle is inscribed in a unit square, so the radius of each circle is 1/2. Establish a coordinate system for the entire 3×3 grid, let the lower left corner be (0,0), and the upper right corner be (3,3). The center of the circle in the upper left unit square is (0.5,2.5), and the center of the circle in the lower right unit square is (2.5,0.5). The distance between the two circle centers is sqrt((2.5-0.5)^2+(0.5-2.5)^2)=sqrt(2^2+(-2)^2)=sqrt(8)=2sqrt(2). The shortest distance between the two circles is equal to the center distance minus the sum of the two radii, namely 2sqrt(2)-1.

raw_record.question_text: A $3 \times 3$ field is made up of 9 unit squares. In two of these squares, circles are inscribed as shown in the diagram. How big is the shortest distance between these circles?

method.method_draft: Read from the diagram that the two inscribed circles are in the top-left and bottom-right unit squares of a 3 by 3 grid. Since each circle is inscribed in a unit square, each has radius 1/2. Assign coordinates to the grid, for example corners from (0,0) to (3,3). The top-left circle has center (0.5,2.5), and the bottom-right circle has center (2.5,0.5). Compute the center distance: sqrt((2.5-0.5)^2+(0.5-2.5)^2)=sqrt(2^2+2^2)=2sqrt(2). The shortest distance between two disjoint circles is the distance between centers minus the two radii, so subtract 1/2+1/2=1 to get 2sqrt(2)-1.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as two equal unit-square incircles placed in diagonally opposite corner cells: one in the upper-left cell and one in the lower-right cell. Draw the straight line through the two circle centers; by symmetry/nearest-point geometry, the shortest segment between the circles lies on this line. The center of the lower-right circle is two unit squares to the right and two unit squares below the center of the upper-left circle, so the center-to-center segment is the diagonal of a 2 by 2 square, with length 2sqrt(2). Along this same line, the part inside the first circle from its center to its boundary is 1/2, and the part inside the second circle is also 1/2. Removing these two radius pieces from the full center-to-center line leaves 2sqrt(2)-1.
